notes: TubeRoom 1.2.2: Color loops now react to stronger bass hits. Tune threshold and minimum gap per group, with a live bass meter and Only the biggest preset. Sustained bass and treble do not cycle colors. Existing beat loops upgrade to Big bass hits; Every tube peak remains available. Uses the tube microphone and FFT; keep TubeRoom running on an awake Mac. No firmware changes.

Colors look wrong?

Test pure red, green and blue below. If a primary color is swapped, open that tube’s WLED → Config → LED Preferences and correct the LED type or color order. TubeRoom sends RGB values; the firmware handles the strip’s wiring order. Keep WLED’s current limit enabled.

Tests briefly light the selected tube at 30% brightness, then restore it. Small shade differences can remain between the screen and LEDs.

Microphone setup

Connect reads the installed AudioReactive settings, keeps the microphone pin configuration, sets the selected tube to Send and the other compatible tubes to Receive, and restarts changed controllers. This changes settings only, never firmware. All enabled tubes must support AudioReactive. A working physical microphone must already be configured on the selected tube.

Choose your color

Catch the bigger booms.

Higher = only stronger bass hits. This is a relative level from the tube, not a decibel measurement.

Start the lights to see the tube’s bass level.

Prevents rapid repeat hits. A new bass hit is still required after the gap; this never advances on a timer.

Looks for a strong rise in low bass, then waits for the sound to settle. The tube analyzes the frequencies; TubeRoom filters the reported levels. A kick, bass note or other low-frequency boom can trigger it.

These controls apply to this group’s color loop.

Sound response

All tubes listen to one selected tube’s microphone. Each group can use a different sound effect and intensity.

The color loop has a Big bass hits filter. Its threshold and minimum gap are under Tune bass trigger. A frequency-range filter is not available for the other stock effects. WLED’s “Low bin / High bin” controls in certain effects map sound frequency to color; they do not filter triggers. Peak effects share the sender’s peak detection, so separate bass/treble triggers per group cannot be promised.

Use the effect’s sensitivity or intensity control when available. For microphone gain, noise floor and automatic gain, open the selected tube’s AudioReactive settings:

Open microphone settings ↗

Simple control. Honest limits.

  1. Setup → add tubes and choose Group A or B → Check & save.
  2. Choose a tube microphone → Connect. Controllers may restart briefly.
  3. Select a group, effect and colors → Start lights. Save changes with Apply groups while running.

Fixed, Fade, Pulse, Scroll, Rainbow and Strobe use installed WLED effects. Scroll travels within each tube; it is not BTAir’s fixture-to-fixture chase. Audio flashes are patches of light, not an exact beat strobe. DJ color uses generated colors, not your own beat-triggered color loop.

Color loop → Big bass hits advances through up to 12 chosen colors on stronger low-frequency rises. Tune bass trigger sets the strength threshold and minimum gap for each group. Every tube peak keeps the previous behavior. There is no timer advance; silence or missing audio packets holds the last color. The tube measures the sound; TubeRoom filters its bass data and relays color changes to the groups that triggered. Keep the Mac awake and the launcher running; Safari may close. WLED detects sound peaks, which may not match every musical beat. Closely spaced triggers within 180 ms are ignored to reduce double hits. Slow or unreachable tubes can miss changes. On a timer remains available and runs entirely on WLED using free preset slots 200–250.

Live samples read actual pixels at up to two updates per second when supported. The layout is a visual arrangement; stock WLED does not use these positions for room-wide effects.

The tube captures audio and calculates its frequency spectrum. TubeRoom uses those reported levels to filter bass triggers and sends RGB commands; it does not capture Mac audio or generate pixel frames. Closing Safari or hiding the tab is fine. Stopping TubeRoom or sleeping the Mac pauses beat color changes at the last color. Other onboard effects keep running. After reopening TubeRoom, click Resume beat relay for an existing beat session. Use Blackout to turn them off; Stop & restore returns each tube to its earlier state. Running playlists from before TubeRoom may need to be restarted in WLED.

No controller firmware is installed or modified. Beat mode needs WLED Audio Sync v2, already present in compatible AudioReactive builds. Existing firmware determines the available effects and microphone support.
KEEP YOUR SETUP. GET THE IMPROVEMENTS.

App updates

Checking installed version…

Stop the lights before installing. Your tube connections, layout and colors stay saved. The app restarts automatically. Tube microphone routing stays saved. Choose update files only from this project’s publisher.

Online update source

Once publishing is connected, enter its permanent HTTPS update address here. This is a one-time setting. Updates run app code, so use a source you trust.

If you do not have an address yet, use Install update file. Online checks need internet; lighting control does not.

The previous version is kept for recovery.
